specName: Convention Agents Rebuild — Fix Phantom Implementations
title: rorca-convention-agents-rebuild
_notes: Post-audit rebuild of rorca-convention-agents. The original spec run (883/885) produced phantom implementations — agents committed type-correct stubs that passed tsc but implemented no business logic. This spec rebuilds the most impactful missing pieces: persona files, persona injection, SkillRegistry, LLM-driven matching, UI wiring for CA-015/016/017/018, and MCP HTTP transport. Run AFTER rorca-e2e-sanity to confirm baseline, and run rorca-e2e-journey AFTER this to verify fixes.
_executionOrder: 3rd — after rorca-convention-agents (done) and rorca-e2e-sanity (run first to confirm baseline). Then run rorca-e2e-journey after this spec completes.

userStories.title: Persona File Library — 15 Built-In Personas in .rorca/personas/
userStories.description: Create the persona markdown files that CA-007 and CA-008 were supposed to produce but didn't. Write 15 persona files under `.rorca/personas/` in the Rorca workspace (self-hosted). Directory structure: `_primary/` (architect.md, pm.md, lead-dev.md), `_adversarial/` (red-team.md, assumption-buster.md, devils-advocate.md), `_specialist/` (frontend.md, backend.md, database.md, security.md, sre.md, ux-designer.md, qa.md), `_review/` (spec-writer.md, spec-verifier.md). Each file uses Agent Skills frontmatter (name, description, triggers) followed by a detailed system prompt section defining the persona's perspective, vocabulary, concerns, and review checklist. The `red-team.md` and `assumption-buster.md` adversarial personas are especially important — they should challenge assumptions aggressively. Also create `backend/src/lib/persona-registry.ts`: a `PersonaRegistry` class with `listPersonas()`, `getPersona(name)`, `getPersonaText(name)` methods that read from `.rorca/personas/` in the workspace `cwd`. Register it as a singleton.

userStories.title: Persona Injection in buildPrompt() — execution-engine.ts
userStories.description: Wire persona injection into `buildPrompt()` in `backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts`. The function signature already exists — add logic to: (1) read `story.suggestedPersona` from the spec JSON story object, (2) use PersonaRegistry to load the persona file content from `<cwd>/.rorca/personas/`, (3) inject persona text AFTER the roleSection (AGENTS.md governance) and BEFORE the matched skills, in this order: contextPreamble → mode instruction → agent-specific instructions → roleSection → persona text → skill content → story task. If `story.suggestedPersona` is absent or the file doesn't exist, skip silently. Log `[engine] Injecting persona: <name>` when a persona is loaded. Also add `suggestedPersona?: string` to the UserStory interface in execution-engine.ts.

userStories.title: SkillRegistry — backend/src/lib/skill-registry.ts
userStories.description: Create `backend/src/lib/skill-registry.ts` with a `SkillRegistry` class. This is distinct from the existing context-files skill routes (which are workspace-file management). The SkillRegistry is a catalog layer: it discovers installed skills from `.rorca/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` in a given workspace `cwd`, parses YAML frontmatter (name, description, triggers), and provides a compact catalog string for LLM prompts. Methods: `discover(cwd: string): SkillEntry[]` — scans both skill dirs, parses frontmatter, deduplicates by name. `getCatalogForPrompt(cwd: string): string` — returns compact 'name: description' list (~750 tokens max for 30 skills). `getSkillContent(cwd: string, name: string): string | null` — reads full skill file content. Create `GET /api/skills?workspaceId=<id>` route in `backend/src/routes/skills.ts` and mount in `backend/src/server.ts`. The route returns `{ skills: SkillEntry[] }` from the workspace's skill directories.

userStories.title: LLM-Driven Skill + Persona Matching in Spec Generation
userStories.description: Modify the spec generation prompt in `backend/src/routes/specs.ts` to include the installed skill catalog and persona catalog, then parse `suggestedSkills` and `suggestedPersona` from the LLM output per story. Specifically: (1) After the direction stack is synthesized (before the main LLM call), call `SkillRegistry.getCatalogForPrompt(cwd)` and `PersonaRegistry.listPersonas()` to build catalog strings. (2) Append to the spec gen system prompt: an `=== INSTALLED SKILLS ===` section (skill name: description per line) and an `=== AVAILABLE PERSONAS ===` section (persona name: description per line). (3) Extend the JSON output schema instruction: each story should include `suggestedSkills: [{name, relevance, reason}]` and `suggestedPersona: string`. (4) After parsing the LLM response, strip any `suggestedSkills[].name` values that are not in the installed catalog. (5) Write the updated story objects (with suggestedSkills and suggestedPersona) back to the spec JSON. The workspace cwd is available from `workspace.path`. If no skills or personas are installed, skip the catalog injection gracefully.

userStories.title: CA-017 Fix — Convention Drift Section in Health Dashboard
userStories.description: Add a 'Convention Drift' section to `src/panels/HealthDashboardPanel.tsx`. Read the file first to understand the existing layout (health score, components, charts). Add a new section below the main health components: (1) A 'Convention Drift' card with a 'Run Drift Check' button. (2) On click, call POST /api/workspaces/:id/conventions/drift (new backend route). The backend route runs a basic drift check: reads the workspace's CLAUDE.md + direction stack L3 and compares against key config files (package.json, tsconfig.json, .eslintrc). Returns { driftItems: [{file, convention, actual, severity}], checkedAt }. (3) Display drift results as a list: green checkmark for compliant, amber warning for drift detected. (4) If no drift data yet: 'Run a drift check to compare your codebase against declared conventions.' This is a simplified implementation — full LLM-based drift detection is out of scope.

userStories.title: CA-018 Fix — Multi-Pass Progress UI in Forge Panel
userStories.description: Add multi-pass generation progress to the Forge panel. Find the actual Forge component by checking App.tsx renderPanel('forge') — it likely renders SpecForgePanelPage or similar. Read that file to understand the existing generation progress UI. When `multiPass: true` is in the generation request, the spec gen endpoint performs multiple LLM passes. Add a progress display: (1) A collapsible 'Generation Passes' section that appears during generation. (2) Shows 6 named steps: PM Analysis, Spec Writer, UX Designer, Best Practices, Adversarial Review, Verifier. (3) Each step has a status icon: pending (grey dot), running (spinner), completed (green check), failed (red X). (4) The frontend polls or uses the existing SSE spec generation progress events to update step status. (5) In single-pass mode (default): shows a single progress bar (existing behavior unchanged). The `multiPass` option can be toggled in Forge Advanced Options. Wire the toggle and pass `multiPass: true` in the generate request body. Backend: Add `multiPass` field to the generate request handler and run all 6 passes sequentially if true, emitting WAL progress events between passes.

userStories.title: MCP HTTP Transport — Streamable HTTP at /mcp
userStories.description: Implement MCP Streamable HTTP transport in addition to the existing stdio server. In `backend/src/mcp/` create `http-transport.ts` that sets up an MCP server with HTTP transport using the `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` package. Mount it in `backend/src/server.ts` at `/mcp`. The HTTP MCP server exposes the same 5 tools as the stdio server: `rorca_get_context`, `rorca_generate_spec`, `rorca_list_specs`, `rorca_approve_spec`, `rorca_pipeline_status`. Use the Streamable HTTP transport pattern from the MCP SDK. Add a health endpoint at GET /mcp that returns `{ transport: 'streamable-http', version: '1.0', tools: 5 }`. Update CLAUDE.md MCP section to document the HTTP transport URL. Do NOT remove the existing stdio server — keep both. The HTTP transport allows Claude Code and other MCP clients to connect without installing a local binary.

userStories.title: Sidebar Accessibility — Add <nav> Wrapper
userStories.description: Fix the accessibility gap in `src/components/Sidebar.tsx`: the sidebar uses a plain `<div>` as its root element with no semantic navigation landmark. Wrap `sidebarContent` in a `<nav aria-label="Main navigation">` element. This is a single-element change but important for screen readers and Playwright selectors. Also add `role="navigation"` to the existing mobile `<nav>` element (it already has the tag but not the explicit role). Verify the change doesn't break any existing CSS (the `<nav>` element should be `display: flex flex-col h-full w-full` same as the existing outer div — transfer the className from the div to the nav wrapper, or nest the nav as a wrapper around the div with `className="contents"` to avoid layout changes).
